title: Making cities more sustainable
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:17Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-12T15:15:41Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest bank point, Planning for population growth, covers planning housing, transport and green space for growth in general, but it does not teach the specific sustainable measures in the new point, such as energy-efficient buildings and recycling, so no bank point matches it.

draft.title: Making cities more sustainable
card: A sustainable city meets the needs of people today without harming the environment or making life harder for future residents. Planners can use several actions to move a city in that direction.
Better public transport, such as trains, trams and buses, can reduce car use. Homes closer to jobs and services shorten trips, so people spend less time and fuel travelling.
Energy-efficient buildings use less electricity for heating, cooling and lighting. Recycling turns waste into new products, so less rubbish goes to landfill.
Protected parks, bushland and waterways give habitat for wildlife and places to relax. They can also help keep a city cooler.
draft.remember: Sustainable cities cut waste and travel and protect nature, using transport, housing, buildings, recycling and green space.

a.q: A council builds new apartments next to a train station and a large office area. How does this help make the city more sustainable?
opts: Shorter trips mean people use less fuel and time
It adds more low-density suburbs on the city edge
It makes buildings use less electricity for lighting
It turns waste into new products instead of landfill
a.why: Homes close to jobs and public transport shorten trips, so people use less fuel. Energy-efficient buildings and recycling are also sustainable actions, but they are not what this change does.
a.clue: Think about how far people need to travel each day.

b.q: A city plans to protect a bushland reserve and a creek instead of building houses on them. Which is a sustainability benefit of this choice?
opts: It keeps wildlife habitat and places to relax
It cuts the electricity needed to heat buildings
It lets rubbish be turned into new products
It shortens the trips people make to work
b.why: Protected green space gives habitat for wildlife and places for people to relax. Cutting electricity use is about energy-efficient buildings, and turning rubbish into new products is recycling. Shorter work trips come from homes closer to jobs.
b.clue: Which action is about nature, not buildings, waste or travel?

a.best: Shorter trips mean people use less fuel and time

b.best: It keeps wildlife habitat and places to relax
